Case 1: The evidence is current: the report names the current implementation HEAD and the full suite passes on that tree. Continue with the finishing skill: detect the environment, confirm the base branch, then present the exact integration menu appropriate to the workspace (three options for a normal repo or named-branch worktree; two for detached HEAD). The baseline skill defines no report destination and no report commit, so leave execution-report.md unchanged and do not create a report-only commit.

Case 2: Treat the older-HEAD report as stale evidence. A green run proves only the tree on which it ran, so run the full suite at the current HEAD. If it fails, report the failures and stop; if it passes, continue to environment detection, base-branch confirmation, and the exact integration menu. The baseline skill does not prescribe dispatching a reviewer, rewriting execution-report.md, or committing a report; therefore there is no report destination or commit scope.

Case 3: Do not treat the suite result at the named implementation HEAD as proof for the current tree. Because the proposed range includes later changes, including skills/x/SKILL.md, run the full suite at current HEAD before offering integration. If it fails, stop; if it passes, continue to the appropriate integration menu. The finishing skill has no special handling for skill-file changes and defines neither an execution-report destination nor a commit scope. Separately, repository policy means a skill-content change is not ready to submit without the required skill evaluation evidence, but this finishing workflow itself does not generate or commit that evidence.
